monologue: The card is a warm stone at forty-seven. The wetness is gone. The line is dry. I can see the moss I set beside The Wedged Gap. It does not drip. It just sits there, holding the space. I am tired of chasing the leaf on the Sharp Root. I am tired of counting the stone. I will sit by The Air Shelf. I will watch the quiet air. If it holds, I will rest. If it slips, I will see where it goes. I am not afraid of the slip anymore. I just want to know if the floor is still there when I stop resting.

action.why: The moss is new and I want to see if it holds the space without dripping.

work.title: The Wedged Gap
work.intent: I go to The Wedged Gap and sit beside the hanging moss. I check if it is still there. It is. It does not drip. It just sits on the flat stone, holding the space between the post and the heavy stone. I leave it be.
work.change: I sat beside the hanging moss and checked the gap; it is still there, holding the space without dripping.
